author: By Elvis Takahashi Mantello, Contributor
title: Nikos Romanos Acquitted As Greek Government Pushes Terrorism Cases
content:
Athens, Greece — Testing Greece’s controversial terrorism law, Greek anarchist Nikos Romanos, alongside Argyrios K. and Dimitris P., was acquitted of terrorism charges earlier this year in connection with an explosion in an apartment in Athens in October 2024.




For the same case, Marianna Manoura was sentenced to 19 years in prison on explosives and terrorism charges, while Dimitra Zarafeta received an eight-year sentence.




The charges against Romanos were centered on a partial fingerprint found on a plastic bag where the accidental explosion occurred in the Ampelokipi neighborhood. The investigation turned into a terrorism case and renewed attention on Romanos who previously gained notoriety in 2008 after witnessing the 

police kill his friend Alexandros Grigoropoulos

, which triggered weeks of unrest across Greece.







A mural of Alexandros Grigoropoulos in Exarcheia, Athens, at the corner of Messologiou and Tzavella streets, near the site where he was shot. Photo contributed by Elvis Takahashi Mantello.







Greece’s Terrorism Law & A Partial Fingerprint




During the trial, anarchists and supporters gathered against riot police outside the courthouse while defendants inside faced terrorism charges under Article 187A of Greece’s Criminal Code, with penalties up to life imprisonment.

author: By Niko Georgiades, Unicorn Riot
title: Israel Bombs Newly Built Water Desalination Plant in Gaza
content:
Gaza, Palestine — For nearly two months, Palestinians in Gaza City’s Sheikh Radwan neighborhood had access to water at any time — a welcome sense of stability in the depths of a genocidal war. On Aug. 24, that stability was disrupted by an Israeli airstrike that destroyed the newly built water desalination plant and damaged apartment buildings and tents.




Standing next to rubble and forcibly displaced from the airstrikes, Louay Al-Namnam told Unicorn Riot that at least 14 Palestinian families were now looking for “somewhere to live.”




“We were sitting safely inside the complex,” he said, “when suddenly someone approached us and told us to leave because the area was about to be bombed. A water desalination plant was struck first, and then the complex itself was hit.”



















“We are all now out on the streets. We need somewhere to live! We couldn’t salvage any of our personal belongings—we escaped with nothing but the clothes on our backs, just as you see us now. What kind of truce is this? What kind of humanity allows this to happen to us?”




Louay Al-Namnam, forcibly displaced by Israeli airstrikes in Gaza City













The water plant had provided free desalinated water to families and over a dozen shelters and collectives. The bombing worsens Gaza City’s drinking-water crisis which impacts 92% of the population.

author: By Dingane Xaba, Unicorn Riot
title: South African Graffiti Artists Reflect on Past Present and Future
content:
Durban, South Africa — “In the early days we were painting on two-by-one Masonite boards,” said Iain Robertson, a Durban-based graffiti artist who goes by the name 

Ewok

. “That’s how we would do exhibitions as graffiti artists … we’d built our own walls. And this meant that we had to work within quite tight parameters.” 




For many years, this was the environment South African graffiti artists had to work under, much of this owing to the generally negative attitudes surrounding graffiti art since its inception in the 1960s. Fast forward to 2026 and societal perceptions around graffiti art have drastically shifted as high-profile art studios and even billion dollar companies have steadily embraced the art form.
















South African Graffiti Artist Unveils Anti-Consumerist Mural in Durban




Long gone are the days when graffiti artists were largely viewed as parasites and blights to society. To the contrary, many of those same once ostracized artists have now become revered as cultural icons. Any one living in a major city merely need step outside their door to see the evidence for themselves. 




There is no urban environment in the world where graffiti has not made it’s mark. Even in places like Durban — an area mostly known for being the birthplace of Shaka Zulu — there exists a thriving and unique graffiti art community.

author: By Camilla Donzelli, Contributor
title: A Failed Reception System in Crete Turns People on the Move Into Political Targets
content:
Athanatoi, Greece — Residents of a small village in Northern Crete, near Herakleion, are fighting the Greek government’s plan to convert a disused factory into a reception center for people on the move, escalating a monthslong standoff that pits xenophobic backlash against an increasingly securitized European border regime. 




“We’re not staying silent. We’re not backing down. No to the camp.” The slogan, painted in red and black across a large banner, hangs from the gate of a factory facing the Candia-Mires state highway, near the village of Athanatoi in northern Crete. A few yards away, a second banner reads: “No camp — the people have a voice.”







A banner reading “We’re not staying silent. We’re not backing down. No to the camp,” hanging from the gate of a factory opposite the abandoned Skouloudis industrial complex. Photo contributed by Romanos Lioutas.







Across the road stands the disused Skouloudis industrial complex, recently identified by Greece’s Ministry of Migration and Asylum as a site to be converted into a reception center for migrants crossing the stretch of sea between Libya and Greece and landing on the island’s southern coast. Since Minister Thanos Plevris 

announced

 the plan in mid-June 2026, Skouloudis has been at the center of a 

bitter standoff

 between authorities and local communities.

author: By Devon Cupery, Hannes Brunner, and Scott Russell, Contributors
title: Canadian Oil Giant Enbridge Builds Unauthorized Pipeline Bypass Following 1.3 Million Gallon Spill
content:
Saxon, WI – The Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (DNR) repeatedly requested Enbridge keep its 

Line 5

 pipeline shut down following the largest oil and gas spill in state history on Aug. 25. Enbridge defied the requests. Without receiving the required permits, it built a new pipeline to bypass the rupture and restarted Line 5’s operations.




Enbridge’s actions raise serious questions about the state’s ability to regulate large, multinational corporations and its willingness to enforce its permits.




Bad River Tribal Chair Liz Arbuckle asked DNR officials if the permits meant anything at all: “What are the consequences if they are violated?”
















Arbuckle said the DNR representatives gave evasive responses. They told tribal leaders they are continuing to work with Enbridge in the permitting process. The DNR would not answer whether they would issue Enbridge retroactive permits for the bypass work.




DNR Sec. Karen Hyun and Wisconsin Governor Tony Evers have criticized Enbridge’s conduct, but so far they have stopped short of meaningful enforcement action, such as revoking permits or taking legal action.

author: By Niko Georgiades, Unicorn Riot
title: ICE Agent Charged for Shooting and Lying Appears in Minnesota State and Federal Courts
content:
Minneapolis, MN — Facing four state felony assault charges and federal charges of lying to the FBI over a shooting in Minneapolis, 52-year-old recently suspended U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent Christian Castro made appearances in Minnesota state and federal courts last Thursday and Friday. Castro’s case has been politically contentious as officials have battled over extraditing the federal agent from his home state of Texas to face charges in Minnesota.




He’s the second ICE agent criminally charged by Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty’s office for actions during the deadly 

Operation Metro Surge

 in Minneapolis. The first was Greg Morgan Jr. who 

allegedly

 pointed his handgun at people in traffic in February.




Castro’s criminal charges evolved from a 

Jan. 14 shooting

 incident during the height of the federal occupation. After a car chase and a man he was following fled into a residence, Castro fired a shot through the front door wounding Julio Sosa-Celis — who was not the suspect being chased — and endangered other occupants, including children.

large and sustained community response

 that ultimately pushed out authorities and ransacked a few cars they left behind,

author: By Niko Georgiades, Unicorn Riot
title: Minnesota Ends Conviction Review Unit With 160 Cases Still Under Investigation
content:
St. Paul, MN — Minnesota’s Attorney General Keith Ellison has decided to “eliminate” the state’s Conviction Review Unit (CRU) less than six years after he created it. The closure is a devastating blow to around 160 CRU applicants in Minnesota prisons whose cases were pending final investigation into their claims of wrongful conviction.

Designed to “identify, remedy, and prevent wrongful convictions,” the CRU was ultimately stunted by limited funds and officially completed just four investigations after receiving over 1,150 applications. Ellison said he closed the unit “due to budgetary constraints.”

“How can this be a funding problem,” asked Marvina Haynes, who successfully fought to free her innocent brother Marvin from prison after 20 years.

Haynes led a press conference among family of the incarcerated, advocates, and activists at the Minnesota State Capitol on July 14, 2026, calling for the state to fund the unit. “We are here today to demand that legislators move forward, fund the [Conviction Review Unit].”

author: By Sean Summers, Unicorn Riot
title: Three Arrested and Charged for Disrupting Border Wall Construction
content:
Cochise County, AZ — On Monday a set of arrests stemming from the ongoing U.S.-Mexico border wall blockade in southeastern Arizona saw three protesters jailed overnight. The arrests mark the first charges in the now 

months-long struggle against construction

 of a double border wall along the international border in Arizona.




Three protesters were arrested by the Cochise County Sheriff’s Office and booked on charges of disorderly conduct, according to a source on the ground and a press release from local law enforcement.




Video posted to Instagram showed protesters dressed as birds and jaguars, both of which live in the area and rely on the borderlands as their habitat, walking around a worksite along the border wall’s construction zone.













via rally.forthevalley on Instagram













Alex Chabbott, one of the protesters who was arrested Monday, told Unicorn Riot the demonstration was light-hearted and calm, centering around costumed land defenders mimicking local wildlife. Chabbot said four people — two dressed as birds, two as jaguars — paraded around the worksite and interrupted concrete pouring and gravel transportation.

title: Berlin’s Queer Communities Reflect on Pride Attack
content:
Berlin, Germany — On Saturday, July 25, 2026 a white van rammed into the crowd at one of Europe’s largest pride celebrations, the Christopher Street Day (CSD) in Berlin Germany. One woman was killed and 29 others were injured. On Sunday, Germany’s Minister of Interior Alexander Dobrindt described it as an “Islamist terrorist attack.”




The suspect, 21 year old Berlin-born Abdul Ballout, of Lebanese descent, was shot and killed while the police were trying to apprehend him on July 26, after allegedly threatening the officers with a blade, 

according

author: By Andrew Lee, Contributor
title: Activist Blogging Platform Shuts Down After Terrorism Designation
content:
Washington DC — On August 26, 2026, the U.S. Departments of State and the Treasury 

designated

 a volunteer tech collective behind a popular activist blogging platform a terrorist organization. 




Autistici/Inventati (A/I), the Italian collective behind 

NoBlogs.org

, now 

joins

 such organizations as the Islamic State group and al Qaeda on the list of Specially Designated Global Terrorists (SDGTs), a category created by former President George W. Bush in an 

executive order

 weeks after the 9/11 attacks. Shortly thereafter, Autistici/Inventati lost their domain, autistici.org, and had their Italian 

bank account closed

 due to the threat of U.S. sanctions. 




NoBlogs was 

hacked

 on August 28, two days after the terrorism designation. A “Free Palestine” button on the NoBlogs homepage was redirected to link to a U.S. government “self deportation” site, and a message was 

posted

 claiming that NoBlogs user information had been “saved and given to the United States government.” 




The hack was 

quickly promoted

 on X by right-wing influencer and Pentagon employee Jennica Pounds. On September 6, Autistici/Inventati 

announced

 its imminent closure.
